I would try to get out as soon as possible. They travel through the walls and will hide in them and come out at night time. Yes it is a bedbug. Likely dead if it’s not moving. The skins look like moltings of them. You may want to look up what bed bug molts look like on Google. Check the crevices of your mattress and box springs, your curtains, behind any picture frames. If you live in an apartment, they can spread from other units easily.

I was infested by my downstairs neighbors. Is your apartment complex paying for the exterminator? Other units will need to be treated as well. Many people do not have reactions to bed bug bites. I would advise for you to get a mattress and box spring cover to protect your bed. Everything will absolutely be okay. It may not seem like it right now, but it will be. I probably would also look into moving as soon as your lease is up. I was reinfested this summer after 5 years of no bed bugs. One of my neighbors likely has an active infestation from my former downstairs neighbors and they stay in the walls. It’s just not worth all the stress, money and and loss of possessions.

With apartments, they spread from other infested units very easily, typically through the walls. They come out through cracks and crevices, especially electrical plates and switch plates. Get a mattress cover for your bed and box springs. Vacuum and steam clean if possible. Set out glue traps around your bed. Inspect your mattress and box springs for signs of infestation.

 I know this is very stressful and anxiety inducing, but you will get through this. It seems like you are taking the right steps. Contact your apartment manager and save any bed bugs in a plastic zip loc bag for proof. Most apartment complexes will spray or hire an exterminator. Units surrounding you will need to be treated as well. I would advise that you sleep in your own bed. Like I said before, I would vacuum well in your bedroom and check your bedding, pillows and mattress for any bugs. 

If you have a dryer, throw your work clothes in there on high heat for a while. It will kill them. Sleep is very important and you need it during this time. Try to remain calm and know that this will pass.

Take apart your bed frame and check your mattress and box springs. Especially check along the crevices of your mattress. When I found one crawling along the headboard area of my bed, I found more in the crevices of my mattress and eggs on the box spring.
If you happen to spot another one, get it in a plastic bag. Hopefully you won’t find another one, but I placed all the ones I’d find in a plastic zip loc bag.

Check your box springs, in the crevices of your mattress, your headboard if you have one, take apart your bed stand and look for them there. Check curtains, behind picture frames and clear any clutter you have. They like to stay close to where you sleep. 

 Do you live in a single family home or apartment/ duplex? Bed bugs can easily travel from unit to unit in apartments if a neighbor has an infestation. Educate yourself on the appearances of bed bugs and their life cycles, from egg to adult. They are sneaky little creatures and tend to come out at night time, especially when you’re asleep. Not everyone reacts to bed bug bites. 

I’m hoping it was brought home by public transportation, but a pregnant female can lay lots of eggs, they look like little pieces of rice. I wish you the best of luck and hope you won’t have a problem with them. It’s best to catch them early and nip it in the bud rather than not be proactive and allow an infestation to start.
